title: Films and Books I Love
paragraphs: Kamila Seitkali loves stories — in any form. She is the kind of person who always has a book in her bag and who cries during films. For her, books and films are not just entertainment; they are windows into other lives, cultures, and ways of thinking.

Her favourite book is 'The Kite Runner' by Khaled Hosseini, a novel that tells the story of a friendship that is tested by betrayal and redemption. 'It's a book that changed the way I think about loyalty and forgiveness,' she says. 'I recommend it to everyone.'

In terms of films, Kamila loves 'October Sky', a true story about a boy who dreams of becoming a rocket scientist despite growing up in a coal-mining town. 'It's a film that shows you can achieve anything if you believe in yourself,' she explains.

Amir Bekzhanov prefers science fiction. His favourite novel is Isaac Asimov's 'Foundation', a series that explores the fall of a galactic empire. 'It's a book that makes you think about civilisation, history, and the power of knowledge,' he says.

Zhibek is passionate about documentaries. She recently watched 'The Social Dilemma', a documentary that examines the impact of social media on mental health and democracy. 'It's a film that everyone should watch,' she says firmly.

At WKU, Dr. Akhmetov encourages students to read widely. 'Read books that challenge you,' he says. 'A book that makes you uncomfortable is often the book that changes you the most.' He believes that students who read regularly develop stronger analytical and communication skills.
